narrationScript: Welcome to Chapter 4.4: File I/O and Exception Handling. In the world of programming, your applications rarely live in a vacuum. They constantly need to interact with external resources, and one of the most common is the file system. Whether it's reading configuration, saving user data, or processing large datasets, File Input/Output, or I/O, is an absolutely critical skill for any developer. But what happens when things go wrong? Files might not exist, network connections might drop, or users might enter invalid data. This is where Exception Handling comes in, allowing your programs to gracefully recover from unexpected events rather than crashing. By the end of this chapter, you'll be able to effectively read and write data to text files using Python’s powerful tools, including the safe and efficient `with` statement. You'll also learn to anticipate and manage common runtime errors using `try`, `except`, `else`, and `finally` blocks, making your Python programs robust and reliable. Let’s dive in!
